Factor 1: Degree of Annexation

The first factor is the Degree of Annexation. This is a factual assessment of how the item is attached.

How stable is it?

Is the attachment firm and secure, or loose and temporary?

How easily can it be removed?

Does removal require specialized tools or significant effort?

Would removal cause significant damage?

Would it leave a large hole in the property or destroy the item itself?

Question 1 of 5MCQ-FRE_7VEXWTPreviousNext
An associate broker in Alberta is charged with a criminal offence that is unrelated to their real estate business. According to the Real Estate Act Rules, what is this individual's notification requirement to RECA?
No notification is required because the charge is not related to their real estate activities.
They are only required to notify the Executive Director if they are convicted.
They must immediately notify the Executive Director of the charge.
They must notify the Executive Director within 30 days of the charge.
SubmitDon't know
Scope & Responsibilities QuizExit
12345
Question 1 of 5MCQ-FRE_7VEXWTPreviousNext
An associate broker in Alberta is charged with a criminal offence that is unrelated to their real estate business. According to the Real Estate Act Rules, what is this individual's notification requirement to RECA?
No notification is required because the charge is not related to their real estate activities.
They are only required to notify the Executive Director if they are convicted.
They must immediately notify the Executive Director of the charge.
They must notify the Executive Director within 30 days of the charge.
Proceed
Explanation
Notes
Topic Targeted

(Correct) They must immediately notify the Executive Director of the charge.

Section 40(1)(a) of the Real Estate Act Rules states that an industry member must immediately give the Executive Director written notice after being charged with an offence under the Criminal Code (Canada) or other similar legislation.

(Incorrect) They are only required to notify the Executive Director if they are convicted.

The Real Estate Act Rules require notification upon being charged, not upon conviction. This ensures RECA is aware of any situation that may affect an industry member's suitability to trade in real estate as soon as it arises.

(Incorrect) They must notify the Executive Director within 30 days of the charge.

The timeline required by the Real Estate Act Rules is "immediately," not within 30 days.

(Incorrect) No notification is required because the charge is not related to their real estate activities.

The requirement to notify RECA applies regardless of whether the criminal charge is related to the individual's real estate business, as any criminal charge pertains to their character and suitability for licensing.

Key Terms
Broker

Pacing Stages

Pacing shows whether you're on track to be ready by your target exam date. It moves through three stages as your mastery grows:

Launch

Get early momentum, level up your first concepts to Intermediate, building to 5 to complete Launch.

Study You're here

Pace every concept toward two targets: Intermediate+ first, then Proficient, before exam day.

Final Review

Prove you're ready by passing full practice exams before test day.

In the Study stage you can switch tabs:
Forward Pacethe daily pace needed from today to hit each target.
Track Pace PREMIUMsee if your real study pace will get you ready in time, or whether you need to pick it up.

A real estate professional is analyzing the detached home market in a specific Alberta city. Over the last three months, they observed the following trends: the sales-to-new-listings ratio has dropped from 80% to 55%; total active listings have increased by 20%; the average days on market has remained low at 25 days; and benchmark prices have continued to increase, but at a slower rate than before. Based on this combination of indicators, what is the most accurate explanation for the current market shift?
The market is stagnant, as indicated by the conflicting signals between sales ratios and pricing trends.
The market has quickly shifted into a buyer's market due to the significant increase in active listings.
The market is decelerating from a strong seller's market toward a more balanced condition.
The market remains a strong seller's market because properties are still selling quickly.

Concept: Scope & Responsibilities

You took 0 seconds on this question.
An associate broker in Alberta is charged with a criminal offence that is unrelated to their real estate business. According to the Real Estate Act Rules, what is this individual's notification requirement to RECA?
No notification is required because the charge is not related to their real estate activities.
They are only required to notify the Executive Director if they are convicted.
They must immediately notify the Executive Director of the charge.
They must notify the Executive Director within 30 days of the charge.
Explanation
Notes
Topic Targeted

(Correct) They must immediately notify the Executive Director of the charge.

Section 40(1)(a) of the Real Estate Act Rules states that an industry member must immediately give the Executive Director written notice after being charged with an offence under the Criminal Code (Canada) or other similar legislation.

(Incorrect) They are only required to notify the Executive Director if they are convicted.

The Real Estate Act Rules require notification upon being charged, not upon conviction. This ensures RECA is aware of any situation that may affect an industry member's suitability to trade in real estate as soon as it arises.

(Incorrect) They must notify the Executive Director within 30 days of the charge.

The timeline required by the Real Estate Act Rules is "immediately," not within 30 days.

(Incorrect) No notification is required because the charge is not related to their real estate activities.

The requirement to notify RECA applies regardless of whether the criminal charge is related to the individual's real estate business, as any criminal charge pertains to their character and suitability for licensing.

Key Terms
Broker
Riley

professionalism. They don't want to wait until a court case is finished, which can take months or years, to be informed. As a self-regulated professional, you have a "duty to report" yourself the moment a formal charge is laid, even if it has nothing to do with buying or selling houses.

For your exam, remember these two specific triggers:

  1. The Timing: It must be immediate.
  2. The Stage: It is upon being charged, not just if you are convicted.

Memory Tip: "The Immediate Alarm"
Think of a criminal charge like a smoke alarm in your professional life. You don't wait to see if the house burns down (the conviction) before calling for help; you have to report the "smoke" (the charge) immediately so the regulator can investigate the situation right away.

Give me one short check-your-understanding question about that distinction. Let me answer before you explain.

To test your understanding of this notification rule, consider this scenario:

An associate is charged with a serious offence under the Criminal Code on a Tuesday. The associate's lawyer tells them they have a very strong case and will likely be found "not guilty" at a hearing scheduled for the following month.

Based on the Real Estate Act Rules, when is the associate required to provide written notice of this charge to the Executive Director?
